# The chain from nitrogen to fedtemøg

*Generated by `scripts/causation.py` from `data/manual/`, `data/derived/` and pinned documents.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-INTRO">Companion to [NITROGEN.md](NITROGEN.md), which audits the nitrogen share where it is made. This page grants the share and asks what connects it to the outcome people name.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-INTRO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The claim, as it is made

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FEDT-DEF">*Fedtemøg* is a popular name for mass occurrences of loose-lying filamentous brown algae that can lie rotting at the water's edge and on the beach ([Danish Wikipedia](https://da.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedtem%C3%B8g)).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FEDT-DEF "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PUBLIC">In the public record this project pinned, that outcome is joined to agriculture's nitrogen:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PUBLIC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-WIKI-AGRI">"Forekomsten af fedtemøg ved danske kyster skyldes især landbrugets udledning af kvælstof" — the same article</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-WIKI-AGRI "What this claim rests on")</sup>
>
> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-DN">"År efter år har vi set forfærdeligt iltsvind og fedtemøg. Skal havet have en chance, må landbrugets kvælstofforurening ned." — Maria Reumert Gjerding, president of Danmarks Naturfredningsforening, on the nitrogen agreement</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-DN "What this claim rests on")</sup>
>
> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-DANVA">Agriculture alone accounts for [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% of nitrogen discharged — DANVA, citing data from Miljøstyrelsen and Aarhus University</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-DANVA "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-JOIN">Put together, a share of nitrogen discharged is joined to an outcome on the shore. Nobody quoted here multiplies the two, but the argument invites the reader to. This page asks what connects them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-JOIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 1. What the number is a share of

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-SCOPE">The [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% is agriculture's share of nitrogen **discharged to coastal waters by source** — the land-based waterborne term, nitrogen arriving at the coast through Danish streams and unmonitored catchments. Those are two rows of the [20](SOURCES.md#F-5a36ae8ceb) this project enumerates in NITROGEN.md:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-SCOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| Row | kt N/yr | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Danish land via monitored streams | [32](SOURCES.md#F-ca904caa01) – [38](SOURCES.md#F-b26e8aa3c1) | Partly Measured |
| Danish land via unmonitored catchments | [27](SOURCES.md#F-c83b4d6327) – [33](SOURCES.md#F-f693b34ac5) | Modelled |
| **The term the percentage divides** | **[59](SOURCES.md#F-33a12f031b) – [71](SOURCES.md#F-2cc3054929)** | |
| **[69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% of it — the agricultural load** | **[41](SOURCES.md#F-1d80559c13) – [49](SOURCES.md#F-546d1f62e4)** | |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-AGRILOAD">So the agricultural part of that term is roughly **[41](SOURCES.md#F-1d80559c13)–[49](SOURCES.md#F-546d1f62e4) kt N/yr** on this project's bounds. That is a real quantity and it is not small. The question is what it is a share *of*.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-AGRILOAD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FLOOR">The enumerated pathways that carry any number sum to **[167](SOURCES.md#F-ed6aa15749) – [327](SOURCES.md#F-bc179fad94) kt N/yr**, with **[10](SOURCES.md#F-27c64403ba) of [20](SOURCES.md#F-5a36ae8ceb) rows empty**. An empty row can only add, so the sum is a floor on the denominator, and a share computed against it is a **ceiling, not an estimate**:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FLOOR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-CEILING">On this project's own bounds, agriculture accounts for **no more than [30](SOURCES.md#F-0f96452fb9)%** of enumerated reactive nitrogen reaching Danish marine waters — and at the wide end of the bounds as little as [13](SOURCES.md#F-258bfbe96b)%. Filling an empty row lowers that ceiling, unless the register's own notes put the row inside another or make it a timing term, as [LANDBRUG.md](LANDBRUG.md) sets out row by row. The bounds carry no source for each row, so the ceiling is only as good as they are.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-CEILING "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-DIFFERENT">The published [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% and this ceiling are not competing estimates of the same thing. They answer different questions, and only the second is the question an outcome at sea raises.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-DIFFERENT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-DEPOSITION">Two terms set the scale of what the share leaves out. **Atmospheric deposition to Danish marine waters is [45](SOURCES.md#F-967b074b52)–[65](SOURCES.md#F-61a9da50ff) kt N/yr** in this project's register — comparable to the entire land-based term, falling on the water directly, and not a line in the apportionment quoted.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-DEPOSITION "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-REGEN">**Sediment regeneration** is not a source at all in that apportionment, and has no number in this project's register either.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-REGEN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 2. Missing coefficients, reported as one number

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-GRANT">Granting the [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% entirely, here is what it has to pass through to become a statement about fedtemøg:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-GRANT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| Link | Coefficient | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agriculture → the land-based waterborne nitrogen term | [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% | **PUBLISHED** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-L1">A residual: measured-plus-modelled total minus modelled point sources minus modelled background, with a retention uncertainty of [16](SOURCES.md#F-ae67e45764) percentage points in this project's register, which gives no source for it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-L1 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| That term → all reactive nitrogen reaching the sea | no coefficient | **OPEN SET** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-L2">[10](SOURCES.md#F-27c64403ba) of [20](SOURCES.md#F-5a36ae8ceb) enumerated pathways carry no number, among them deposition's organic fraction, submarine groundwater discharge and sediment regeneration.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-L2 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Nitrogen at sea → the growth of the algae | no coefficient | **NOT COMPUTED** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-L3">Growth also needs light, phosphorus, a season and a surface to attach to, and uses nitrogen regenerated in place as well as nitrogen delivered; nothing here says how much of the growth the delivered share accounts for.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-L3 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Growth → fedtemøg on a shore | no coefficient | **NOT MEASURED** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-L4">The strands tear loose, drift and strand, which takes retention, wind and a shore; no shore-condition series was found in any source this project surveyed.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-L4 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-EVERYLINK">Every one of those links is a real causal connection, and none of them has a number here. A product of unknown fractions is an unknown fraction — **not a small one**. Agriculture may still be the largest single contributor at every link; this project has not computed it either way, and no source it holds does.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-EVERYLINK "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 3. Fedtemøg is grown, so nitrogen is on its path

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-GROWN">Fedtemøg is algae, and algae are grown: the strands attach to stones, mussels or other algae and grow on until they tear loose (Danish Wikipedia). So nitrogen is on fedtemøg's path, and the open questions are *which* nitrogen and *what else* limits the growth — not whether nitrogen matters.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-GROWN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### Oxygen depletion has more routes than growth

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-ROUTES">The iltsvind named in the same breath has at least three routes, and nitrogen is a necessary condition for one of them:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-ROUTES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| Route | What arrives | Does it need nitrogen? |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Growth** | dissolved nutrients | **Yes** — this is the modelled pathway |
| **B. Direct organic matter** | organic carbon that is already biomass or was never alive at all — sewage solids, faecal matter, resuspended basin sludge, and fat | **No.** The material does not have to be grown here. It was grown somewhere else, out of somebody else's nitrogen — or, in the case of fat, contains none. |
| **C. Killing what is already there** | nothing — toxicants, hypoxia, sulphide, physical disturbance | **No.** The standing stock of living tissue in a bay is converted to detritus in place. No new carbon enters the system. |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-BC">Routes B and C are not exotic. B is what a combined sewer overflow carries. C is what a hypoxic event or a toxicant pulse does. Neither is a line in the nitrogen apportionment, which counts nitrogen mass.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-BC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The overflow's own carbon

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-TYPETAL-INTRO">The comparison can be made from the nutrient typetal in this project's monitoring register, which give each discharge type both an organic load (COD) and a nitrogen load. Route A's carbon is what that nitrogen could grow at Redfield stoichiometry — [5.68](SOURCES.md#F-8efe9e918d) g C per g N. Route B's carbon is what the water already carries — [0.375](SOURCES.md#F-74df7a34c3) g C per g COD.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-TYPETAL-INTRO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| Discharge type | COD mg/l | Tot-N mg/l | **B: carbon delivered** | **A: carbon its N could grow** | B ÷ A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Combined sewer overflow | [180](SOURCES.md#F-ab2f9e3892) | [12.0](SOURCES.md#F-939768acc0) | [68](SOURCES.md#F-d0101bc26f) mg C/l | [68](SOURCES.md#F-6e395085a5) mg C/l | **[0.99](SOURCES.md#F-c9a63df6ef)** |
| Separate stormwater | [50](SOURCES.md#F-c8223c7abc) | [2.0](SOURCES.md#F-2ca33c49e9) | [19](SOURCES.md#F-d0c83c37a9) mg C/l | [11](SOURCES.md#F-a2696b3aca) mg C/l | **[1.65](SOURCES.md#F-58176f5f9a)** |
| Stormwater runoff (reference) | [160](SOURCES.md#F-c77ebc5d53) | [10.0](SOURCES.md#F-558b2b44a9) | [60](SOURCES.md#F-a4d62aee29) mg C/l | [57](SOURCES.md#F-a99e154c67) mg C/l | **[1.06](SOURCES.md#F-f642509b7d)** |
| Raw sewage (reference) | [320](SOURCES.md#F-7ce072cf5f) | [43.0](SOURCES.md#F-7d3c1096b2) | [120](SOURCES.md#F-da84b98e4f) mg C/l | [244](SOURCES.md#F-f215135964) mg C/l | **[0.49](SOURCES.md#F-947e7046c7)** |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-CSO">A combined sewer overflow carries **[68](SOURCES.md#F-d0101bc26f) mg of organic carbon per litre directly**, and enough nitrogen to grow **[68](SOURCES.md#F-6e395085a5) mg C/l** — a ratio of **[0.99](SOURCES.md#F-c9a63df6ef)**. The two routes are the same size. The nitrogen apportionment counts only the second, and in this project's register the overflow's nitrogen is [0.6](SOURCES.md#F-2a17fa5268)–[0.7](SOURCES.md#F-db2b4d8e7a)% of the land-based term.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-CSO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-OTHERS">For separate stormwater and for the stormwater-runoff reference the direct term is the *larger* of the two. Only raw sewage — the one stream that goes to treatment — is nitrogen-dominated.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-OTHERS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-CEILINGS">*Both columns are ceilings.* Not all COD is degradable on a relevant timescale, and not all nitrogen is assimilated. The two overstatements run in the same direction, so the **ratio** is the robust part; the absolute milligrams are not.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-CEILINGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FAT">Part of what an overflow carries is fat, which contains **[0](SOURCES.md#F-5ef28a7f0b)%** nitrogen and takes **~[2.9](SOURCES.md#F-4f7a64285f) g <span class="chem" data-chem="O2" title="oxygen (dissolved, as a molecule)">O₂</span> per g** to oxidise, against ~[1.1](SOURCES.md#F-83920f4ca4) for carbohydrate: a nitrogen account cannot see it at all.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FAT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### Why the direct route acts differently

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PG-1">**Route A carbon is conditional.** It requires a phototroph that is present, in a growing season, with light reaching it, and with phosphorus and silicon in supportive ratio. Nitrogen delivered in November grows little.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PG-1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PG-2">**Route B carbon is unconditional.** It is already organic matter. It settles, it decays, and it consumes oxygen in the dark in December as well as in July.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PG-2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PG-3">**Route B arrives where it is discharged.** Route A carbon is produced wherever the light and the season allowed, which may be nowhere near the shore that receives the consequence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PG-3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PG-4">**Route B arrives in pulses, on the flow threshold** — the same events that scour a basin and resuspend its accumulated sludge. Route A is a slower background.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PG-4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-SEASON">So for oxygen the two routes keep different calendars: nitrogen's effect on growth is highest in spring and summer and small in late autumn, while direct organic matter acts year-round and arrives whenever the rain falls.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-SEASON "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-ROUTEC">**Route C needs no input term.** A bay holds a standing stock of living tissue — macroalgae, eelgrass, fauna, biofilm. Kill it and that tissue becomes detritus without a single additional gram entering the system; a toxicant pulse, a hypoxic event, a sulphide pulse and a trawl all do this. It can explain why a bay produces more decaying material in a year when *less* was delivered to it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-ROUTEC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-CONSEQUENCE">**The consequence for the [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)%.** For fedtemøg, which is grown, nitrogen is on the path and the question is how much of the nitrogen growing it is agriculture's. For iltsvind, removing nitrogen would close route A and leave routes B and C running.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-CONSEQUENCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 4. How much of a bloom was delivered

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-LOOP">There is a second structural problem, and it does the most damage to an apportionment: the system feeds itself. Simple, fast-replicating life grows on whatever is available; its respiration and decay draw the oxygen down; things that need oxygen die — fauna, and then everything else; the dead tissue remineralises, releasing the nutrients it was built from; and those nutrients feed the first step again, with less competition for them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-LOOP "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-LOOP-EASIER">Every turn of that loop makes the next easier, and the material driving it from the second turn on was **already in the bay**. It is not a delivery; nothing crossed a boundary an accounting could meter.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-LOOP-EASIER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-NEWREGEN">Marine biogeochemistry separates **new production**, running on nutrients newly supplied to the productive layer, from **regenerated production**, running on nutrients recycled in place; their ratio is the f-ratio.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-NEWREGEN "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FRATIO">How much of a Danish coastal bloom runs on regenerated nitrogen is not established here. The article pinned associates high f-ratios with productive systems dominated by large phytoplankton, and low ones with low-biomass, oligotrophic food webs.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FRATIO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-MINORITY">Where most of a bloom's nitrogen is regenerated, attributing the bloom to a share of delivered nitrogen is a statement about the minority term: the rest was released by an earlier round of dying, not delivered that summer.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-MINORITY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### What the loop does to the arithmetic

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-LINEAR">An apportionment is a linear instrument. It assumes the outcome is a weighted sum of the inputs, so that halving one input removes its share of the outcome. A self-amplifying loop is not a weighted sum. In one:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-LINEAR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-AR-1">**the trigger and the fuel are different quantities.** External input can be small and still start something that runs on internal stock;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-AR-1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-AR-2">**the same input produces different outcomes** depending on how far round the loop the system already is — the state-dependence of section 7, arriving by a second route;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-AR-2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-AR-3">**there are thresholds.** Below one, the loop damps; above it, the loop runs. Attribution either side of that line means different things;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-AR-3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-AR-4">**history matters.** What is in the sediment was delivered in earlier years, and it is released on the sediment's schedule, not this year's.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-AR-4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FEEDBACK">That is the ordinary behaviour of a system with positive feedback.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FEEDBACK "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-DCE-WEATHER">DCE's own notes explain how an iltsvind season develops by the weather of the year: wind that mixes the water column slows it, and high water temperature promotes it, because oxygen consumption rises with temperature and oxygen's solubility falls.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-DCE-WEATHER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### A start further along the loop

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-E5">The register's [E5](HYPOTHESES.md "Direct chemical oxygen demand of discharges") proposes a different start: a bay receiving a large, pulsed delivery of sewage solids and fat can enter the loop further along — the organic material and the oxygen demand arrive together, already made, and the die-off that releases the internal store can be the *first* step. Whether that happens in Køge Bugt is not tested here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-E5 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-E5-SHAPE">It is a different causal shape from the one the accounting models, it could produce the same shore, and any method that counts only nitrogen would attribute it to nitrogen.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-E5-SHAPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 5. The test that has already been run

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-TEST">There is one empirical check on the nitrogen-dominant model, and Denmark has spent more than three decades running it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-TEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-REDUCTION">**The intervention.** DCE's national runoff report puts the reduction in nitrogen supply from land to Danish coastal waters between 1990 and 2018 at [51](SOURCES.md#F-f3813ac6c6)%, calculated on discharge-weighted mean annual concentrations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-REDUCTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-OUTCOME">**The outcome.** When DCE reported the September 2023 extent of oxygen depletion it was the second largest registered. September 2024's was [11,000](SOURCES.md#F-219d622646) km², nearly [50](SOURCES.md#F-1615595b34)% larger than 2023's, and again the second largest registered, exceeded only by 2002.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-OUTCOME "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-JUXTA">**Put side by side:** the land-based supply roughly halved, and the 2024 September extent was the second largest registered. If load were the dominant control on oxygen depletion, halving it should have moved the extremes; these years do not show that it has — and two years are not a test. Section 9 says what would be.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-JUXTA "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-WEATHER">On DCE's own account the extremes follow the weather of the year, with load as a slower background. That is also why a load series computed to take the weather out cannot be read against them year by year.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-WEATHER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 6. Three ways to explain the gap

| Explanation | Standing | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy lag | **PARTIAL** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-LAG">DCE attribute the drift in their nitrogen models to the time lag of nitrogen accumulated in the sediments; how long the lag is, is not established here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-LAG "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Warming | **SUPPORTED, INDEPENDENT** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-WARMING">DCE's notes: high water temperature promotes iltsvind, because oxygen consumption rises with temperature and oxygen's solubility falls. Temperature is not a line in a source apportionment.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-WARMING "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Loss of assimilative state | **ARGUED, UNQUANTIFIED** | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-STATE">The register's [K12](HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of habitat-forming structure"), [D8](HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of biostabilisation, and the mobile bed") and [T4](HYPOTHESES.md "Marine replant failure: negative sediment feedback") each describe a way the same load could do more damage now than before; none is a line in any account.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-STATE "What this claim rests on")</sup> |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-ONLYFIRST">Only the first leaves the policy frame intact — it says the intervention is working and the answer is patience.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-ONLYFIRST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-NOTSOURCE">The three share a property worth stating plainly: **none of them is a source.** A source apportionment cannot represent a lag, cannot represent temperature, and cannot represent the difference between a bay that can absorb a kilogram of nitrogen and a bay that cannot. They are not omitted because they were judged small. They are omitted because the instrument has no slot of that shape.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-NOTSOURCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-MORE">So when the intervention underperforms, the instrument has one thing it can recommend: more of the same intervention. Not because that is the best reading of the evidence, but because it is the only reading the instrument can express.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-MORE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 7. State-dependence, stated as a hypothesis

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-SUBSIDY">Nitrogen is not a toxicant. It is a growth subsidy. What decides whether a subsidy produces eelgrass meadows or a bacterial mat is **which life is present and able to take it up**, and that is a property of the receiving system, not of the nitrogen.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-SUBSIDY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-FSTATE">So the damage function may be not *f(load)* but *f(load, state)*, with the state term driven down by things that are not nutrients. The register holds each as a hypothesis:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-FSTATE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-S1">toxicants and metals that remove grazers and filter feeders, the organisms that would turn the subsidy into structure ([E15](HYPOTHESES.md "Total biocide load, whatever its source"), [E10](HYPOTHESES.md "Heavy metals"), [K13](HYPOTHESES.md "Food depletion for filter feeders and larvae"));</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-S1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-S2">physical disturbance of the bed, which removes the binding fauna and lets the bed move ([D1](hypodrafts/D1.md "Bottom trawling"), [D8](HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of biostabilisation, and the mobile bed"));</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-S2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-S3">each hypoxic event, which kills the benthos and can make the next event cheaper;</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-S3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-S4">the loss of eelgrass, which removes uptake and sediment stabilisation at once ([K12](HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of habitat-forming structure"), [T4](HYPOTHESES.md "Marine replant failure: negative sediment feedback"));</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-S4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-S5">turbidity from a resuspending bed, which keeps the light from whatever might recolonise ([D7](hypodrafts/D7.md "Storm-driven resuspension"), [K11](HYPOTHESES.md "Light as a depleted resource")).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-S5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-SENS">If they hold, each is a reason the same kilogram of nitrogen does more damage now than it did in 1990, and none appears in a source apportionment, because none is a source. **Nitrogen sensitivity would then be a derived property of a damaged system**, and the accounting treats it as a constant.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-SENS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 8. What this does and does not establish

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-NOTHOOK">**It does not establish that agriculture is off the hook.** Multiplying unknown fractions yields an unknown, not a small one. Agriculture is plausibly still the largest single nitrogen contributor, and the load is real.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-NOTHOOK "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-NOTFAILED">**It does not establish that nitrogen policy failed.** Necessary and insufficient are different findings, and the record is consistent with the second.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-NOTFAILED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-ESTABLISH">**It does establish that the number is not what it is read as.** "[69.6](SOURCES.md#F-e2cc286a52)% of nitrogen" is a residual of models over one term of an open account. Read as a share of fedtemøg, it is multiplied by coefficients nobody here has computed. The first is a defensible piece of bookkeeping. The second is not a measurement of anything.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-ESTABLISH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-ASYMMETRY">**And it shows an asymmetry in what gets counted.** Every term that would shift blame away from a countable source — deposition, regeneration, groundwater, legacy, temperature, state — is a term with no line in the apportionment quoted. That may be coincidence of what is easy to measure. It is worth noticing that the easy measurements and the politically actionable ones are the same set.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-ASYMMETRY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The practical consequence

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-PRACTICAL">If nitrogen were the whole binding constraint, this would be a solved problem in principle: catch crops, wetlands, treatment upgrades and extractive aquaculture are available, and enough has already been deployed to roughly halve the land-based supply. Either the remaining reduction needed is far larger than anything currently proposed, or nitrogen is not the whole binding constraint.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-PRACTICAL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-CANNOT">Both readings sit in the same record. **That the record so far cannot distinguish them is an argument that the accounting measures the wrong thing.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-CANNOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 9. What would separate the readings

| To test | Do this |
|---|---|
| Whether the extremes track load at all | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-T1">Regress annual iltsvind extent on the land-based load, wind work over the stratified season, and the bottom-water temperature anomaly. No published regression of this kind was found in the sources this project holds.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-T1 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Whether state-dependence is real | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-T2">The same regression with an interaction term, or simply: does a given load produce more hypoxia now than in 1990, holding weather constant?</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-T2 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Whether the denominator can be closed | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-T3">Two of the [10](SOURCES.md#F-27c64403ba) empty rows have established methods — submarine groundwater discharge by radon or radium tracers, internal regeneration by benthic flux chambers — and both need new measurements.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-T3 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Whether the potency term matters | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-T4">Weight existing load figures by season and receiving-water stratification. Even a crude weighting beats the current implicit equal weight everywhere.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-T4 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |
| Whether fedtemøg has the season everyone assumes | <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-T5">Fixed coastal cameras and a monthly index, year-round: a new instrument, and the only way the fedtemøg season stops being unfalsifiable in either direction.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-T5 "What this claim rests on")</sup> |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-PC-CA-THREE">Three of the five need no new instrument, only series that exist; the other two need new measurements.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-PC-CA-THREE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
